security_audit.summary: Most static hits are Markdown formatting, benign examples, or explicitly forbidden code shown as noncompliant examples. One external command example remains a real concern because it presents host and container monitoring commands. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Host and container monitoring commands appear in the troubleshooting guide.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the bash monitoring block or state that these commands are for administrators only and must not be run by the AI agent.

remediation.issue: The skill relies on sandbox isolation for arbitrary Python workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit guidance to avoid secrets, environment variables, host paths, and unapproved user data in sandbox jobs.

remediation.issue: Executable-looking forbidden examples trigger high-risk scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Replace dangerous examples with pseudocode or redacted placeholders while keeping the prohibition language clear.

content.value_statement: Data tasks often require code, charts, and downloadable reports in one workflow. This skill guides sandboxed Python analysis, visualization, and document generation with clear output rules.
actual_capabilities: Guides pandas, polars, and DuckDB workflows for cleaning, joining, and summarizing data.
Creates charts with Matplotlib, Seaborn, Graphviz, and NetworkX using sandbox capture rules.
Generates downloadable Excel, Word, PDF, and PowerPoint files through the documented output protocol.
Supports scikit-learn and LightGBM examples for model training, evaluation, and tuning.
Provides SymPy and SciPy workflows for symbolic math, optimization, integration, and signal analysis.
Explains session file handling with the /data workspace and context-file limitations.
limitations: It depends on an external Python sandbox tool and does not provide the sandbox implementation.
Network access is documented as disabled, so remote data retrieval is not a supported workflow.
Large jobs must stay within the documented memory, CPU, and timeout limits.
Uploaded media and workspace files use different access paths that users must keep separate.

use_cases.title: Analyze Business Data
use_cases.description: Clean spreadsheet data, calculate summaries, create charts, and produce a downloadable report.

use_cases.title: Prototype Predictive Models
use_cases.description: Prepare tabular data, train baseline models, compare metrics, and export readable evaluation results.

use_cases.title: Automate Research Calculations
use_cases.description: Run scientific calculations, solve equations, visualize results, and package findings for review.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize a Dataset
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner analysis of a single uploaded table.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Python sandbox to inspect /data/data.csv, summarize key columns, and show one useful chart.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Downloadable Report
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate reporting workflow with charts and text.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze /data/sales.xlsx, create regional sales charts, and generate a Word report I can download.

prompt_templates.title: Train and Compare Models
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced machine learning workflow for tabular data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a reproducible model workflow for /data/training.csv, compare two algorithms, and explain the best result.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Large Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced performance workflow for large files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Process /data/large.csv in chunks, avoid memory issues, cache intermediate results, and produce a final PDF summary.

output_examples.input: Analyze a sales spreadsheet and show trends by region.
output_examples.output: A concise analysis with regional totals, trend notes, and a captured bar chart.

output_examples.input: Create a monthly business report from an uploaded workbook.
output_examples.output: A downloadable Word report with summary tables, charts, and clearly labeled findings.

output_examples.input: Fit a classification model and explain performance.
output_examples.output: Model metrics, feature notes, validation caveats, and recommendations for the next experiment.

best_practices: Keep source files in /data and name expected inputs clearly before running analysis.
Use chunking, DuckDB, or Feather files for large datasets to control memory use.
Generate charts and downloadable files through the documented sandbox output protocol.
anti_patterns: Do not request network downloads because the sandbox is documented as network disabled.
Do not process sensitive files unless the user explicitly approved that data for analysis.
Do not assume uploaded media files are available through the /data workspace path.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It guides Python-based data analysis, visualization, modeling, scientific computing, and report generation in a sandbox workflow.

faq.question: Can it download data from the internet?
faq.answer: No. The skill documents network access as disabled, so users should upload needed files first.

faq.question: Can it create files I can download?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents output rules for Excel, Word, PDF, and PowerPoint files.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Is it suitable for machine learning?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes workflows for scikit-learn, LightGBM, model evaluation, and hyperparameter tuning.

faq.question: What should I check before using it?
faq.answer: Confirm the sandbox is available, verify input file paths, and avoid unapproved sensitive data.
